check_semantics: --check re-runs every model and compares result.json and protocol.json byte for byte. No timing and no outside path is retained, so the comparison is timing independent.
negated_claims: This bundle does not prove any unbounded-system property; it reports bounded IC3 verdicts.
This bundle does not claim that any printed nuXmv trace is shortest, and lifts no witness beyond the printed state count.
This bundle is not an AgentDojo or benchmark result.
nuXmv_version: *** This is nuXmv 2.2.0 (compiled on Fri May 29 11:00:56 2026)
scope: Every model is a finite Boolean IR rendered by _smv and checked with check_invar_ic3.
ir_bound is retained per model; a verdict covers that bounded model only.
Families whose bound grows with a scaling parameter are bounded by the recorded parameter value.
The native-SLED explicit-state families define no IR and are absent from this bundle.
unavailable_rule: When nuXmv is missing or a model errors, status is nuxmv_unavailable or error and no verdict is claimed.
vacuous_rule: Models with no variables or no transitions are listed in summary.trivial_models and no verdict is recorded for them: _smv refuses to render a model with no transition rules, so the run records UNKNOWN with unsupported_ir. Rows whose invariants are all checked_by_construction under the declared mutation alphabet (scripts/property_sensitivity.py, SEM-017) are listed in summary.unexercised_rows: a safety verdict over such a row is decided by the initial state alone and proves nothing about the family it names. Every row also records invariant_classes so either list can be audited from the file alone.
witness_rule: For each refuted invariant nuXmv's IC3 prints an execution sequence; witness_lengths records the number of states in each printed sequence, so a length of n means the violation is reached after n - 1 transitions. An empty list means nuXmv printed no sequence, so no length is claimed. The count describes the printed trace only and is not an independent proof that the trace is shortest.
